title: Vault rotation, break-glass runbook & credential inventory
content:
Purpose:
This working runbook captures the agreed operational procedures for secrets vaulting, automated rotation, break-glass (emergency) access, and the living credential inventory. It is intentionally pragmatic — focused on what on-call and infra engineers actually need to do during routine rotation and during incidents.

Scope and assumptions:
- Primary vault technology: HashiCorp Vault (hvac + Transit/KV). Secondary: AWS Secrets Manager for some AWS-only services, GCP Secret Manager for GCP projects.
- Keys and HSM: Customer KMS/HSM integrations are surfaced via KMS connectors; KMS rotation policy is managed in cloud consoles.
- RBAC v2 note: Secrets access controlled by RBAC v2 roles; role -> Vault policy mapping must be up-to-date in the credential inventory.

Quick concepts:
- TTL vs rotation cadence: TTL is the short-lived token lifetime (minutes->hours). Rotation cadence is the policy frequency for long-lived credentials (days->months).
- Vaulted vs ephemeral: Prefer ephemeral credentials (database dynamic creds, short-lived cloud tokens). Vault stores static secrets only when ephemeral cannot be used.

Credential inventory (living):
- Inventory columns we maintain: credential_id | owner | service | vault_path | rotation_cadence | last_rotated | exposure_score | access_roles | notes
- Example entry (CSV line): cred-db-payments, payment-svc, rds/payments/prod, vault.kv/data/rds/payments, 30d, 2026-02-10, medium, [svc-payments, eng-payments-oncall], uses read-only replica creds for queries
- Ownership: Every credential MUST have a single named owner (person or team contact). If owner unknown -> tag "owner:unknown" and create SEC ticket.

Rotation runbook (routine rotation):
1) Pre-checks (24h before): confirm recent backup of Vault (snapshot exists), ensure CI job for integration tests green (see GH-ops/rotate-scripts), notify service owners via Slack channel #sec-rotate 48h before wide rotations.
2) Validate automation: run local dry-run: ./scripts/rotate.sh --dry-run --credential-id <id> 
   - Expected output: new secret version staged in vault metadata, access tests created, smoke test service token retrieval.
3) Staged rotate (apply new secret, keep old for fallback): 
   - vault kv put <path> value=@new-secret.json metadata.versioned=true
   - update secret-version tag in inventory via ./inventory/update.py --id <id> --last-rotated YYYY-MM-DD
4) Live test: trigger service to consume new secret via staged endpoint or feature flag. Run smoke tests.
5) Cutover: promote new secret as active. Monitor for 60 minutes. If any failures, rollback to previous version (see rollback steps).
6) Post-rotation: update audit ticket and attach evidence (automation logs, smoke test pass/fail, timestamps). Evidence automation should push artifacts to the compliance evidence bucket.

Rollback (if a rotation causes failure):
- Command: vault kv metadata get <path> (find previous version), vault kv put <path> value=@previous-secret.json
- Inform on-call and paging policy. Create incident with tag sec-rotation-failure and include root-cause notes.

Emergency break-glass (when normal SSO/RBAC paths unavailable):
Preconditions: break-glass procedure used only when all normal paths fail and an incident commander authorizes it. Break-glass uses short-lived, tightly scoped credentials with full auditing.
1) Escalation: Incident commander (IC) obtains authorisation from Security Lead + Eng Director (ticket approval). Approval must be recorded in the incident ticket.
2) Generate break-glass token: run from bastion with MFA enforced. Example flow (Vault):
   - one-time HSM-wrapped root token request: python tools/request_breakglass.py --owner <name> --reason "<incident-id>"
   - Token auto-expires after 2 hours by policy.
3) Access log: All break-glass sessions MUST be screen-recorded or use session-manager (SSM) with session recordings stored to the audit bucket.
4) Post-use: Within 24 hours, IC must file a post-mortem and rotate any credentials that were used or touched. The break-glass token is revoked immediately after use.

RBAC v2 interplay notes:
- Mapping: RBAC role names should map to vault policies 1:1. Policy naming convention: rbv2.<role>.vaultpolicy (example: rbv2.sre.vaultpolicy).
- Least privilege: define deny-by-default policies. Use group-to-role sync jobs to keep Vault token creation aligned with SSO groups.
- Periodic review: quarterly role membership audit; owners must attest in the credential inventory.

Audit logs and SIEM export for secrets activity:
- Vault audit devices MUST be enabled for syslog and file. Configure route to our SIEM (Splunk/Datadog). Example: vault audit enable file file_path=/var/log/vault_audit.json format=json
- Key events to export: create/update/delete/restore of secret, token creation/renew/revoke, break-glass-token-issue, policies changed, mount/unmount of secrets engines.
- Audit schema hints: keep these fields to map into SIEM: timestamp, event_type, actor_principal, vault_path, action, request_id, session_id, service_context (service name), ip_address, user_agent, success(boolean), raw_payload.
- Evidence automation: rotation jobs MUST emit a signed manifest: {credential_id, rotation_time, actor, job_run_id, smoke_test_hash, outcome}. The manifest is uploaded to compliance bucket and a pointer is stored in the inventory. (See linked GH-ops/rotate-scripts PR for manifest format).

Operational scripts and automation hooks (notes):
- rotate-scripts repo contains: rotate.sh, validate_rotate.py, aws-syncer, gcp-syncer, inventory/update.py. Use the CI job rotate:daily to test the pipeline on a canary credential.
- CI artifacts push to s3://redwood-sec-evidence/<date>/<job_run_id>.zip and index entry added to inventory as evidence_url.

Ownership and run cadence:
- Short-lived ephemeral creds: rotate via automation; owners review every 90 days.
- Long-lived static creds: rotate every 30 days unless mitigations documented.
- Master keys / signing keys: rotate every 365 days with overlapping rollover and strict HSM processes.

Checklist for on-call when credential alerts fire:
- Confirm the credential id and owner in inventory.
- Check last_rotated and smoke test outcome in evidence store.
- If suspicious: immediately set credential state to "quarantined" in inventory and create SEC ticket.
- If compromised: initiate full rotation and rotate all dependent creds (see dependency graph tool).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Automate role -> vault-policy sync (work in progress; owner: Ravi).
- Add automated exposure_score calc into inventory (owner: Anne-Marie).
- Post-incident: standardize the evidence manifest JSON schema and publish Confluence schema page.

References and quick links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/infa/secrets-lifecycle
- GH-ops: https://github.com/redwood/ops/tree/main/rotate-scripts
- Incident playbook: jira://SEC-2020

Notes to reviewers: this doc is an operational draft. Expect sections to be replaced by formal runbooks in runbooks.redwood once validated by SRE and Security. Add suggested edits inline or ping @maya.
